newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Savimbi quits stalling on Angola unity forum.
newsitem.headline: Savimbi quits stalling on Angola unity forum.

text.p: Angola's rebel UNITA leader, Jonas Savimbi, promised on Monday that all UNITA members of a new unity parliament would be in the capital Luanda in 24 hours, clearing the way for its long-delayed inauguration.

Savimbi, who has been stalling on a commitment to send in UNITA parliamentarians, made his latest pledge after meeting visiting United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan at UNITA's stronghold near Bailundo in central Angola.

Formation of a national unity government is the key final step in a U.N.-brokered 1994 peace pact to end the war between UNITA and the Angolan government. It has been delayed several times, mainly by Savimbi.
"All our remaining deputies will be in Luanda tomorrow morning," the UNITA leader reassured reporters travelling with Annan, who confirmed Savimbi's fresh promise.

"I have had a very good talk with Dr Savimbi and we have agreed that all the remaining deputies will be in Launda tomorrow," Annan said. "So, I will have an opportunity to speak to a unified national assembly."
The U.N. chief was on a four-day visit to Angola, where 7,000 U.N. peacekeeping troops are helping to implement a plan to end Africa's longest civil war.
Part of his mission was aimed at persuading Savimbi to send the last 21 UNITA officials, out of 70, to Luanda as agreed.
Thousands of UNITA supporters lined the dusty road from the airport to Bailundo to greet Annan. Banners with UNITA slogans and signs of welcome were strung across buildings.

Speaking to the crowd from a balcony at UNITA headquarters, Annan said: "Today is a very important day for Angola and the Angolan people. Today we decided to take the final and definitive steps towards the formation of a government of unity and national reconciliation.

Savimbi said that as soon as the UNITA deputies arrived, it would be up to President Jose Eduardo dos Santos to choose the date for the formation of the unity government. That date has been set and changed repeatedly in the past.
Savimbi again made clear, however, that independent Angola's first peace-time government would be inaugurated without him.
"I will not be coming. There are still a number of problems and I want to have them sorted out before I travel to Luanda," he said, declining to elaborate.
However, he went as far as saying he was prepared to meet Dos Santos in Angola to discuss them, rather than in a third country, which was the condition for previous meetings.

UNITA (Union for the Total Independence of Angola) and the government signed the peace pact in neighbouring Lusaka in 1994 to end two decades of war which broke out after independence from Portugal in 1975.
